claims.text: Grants are available to cover tuition fees for eligible undergraduate students in Scotland.
The grants are for the academic year 2026-27.
Eligibility is for individuals from low-income households.
The grants are for those ineligible for tuition fee support from the Scottish Government.
The scheme supports students enrolled on an undergraduate degree course at a Scottish Institute of Higher Education.
The grants cover the cost of tuition fees, up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.
Applicants must demonstrate that their financial circumstances do not allow them to cover the cost of their tuition fees.
Retrospective applications will not be accepted.
Applications will not be accepted if the student has incurred tuition fee debts in a previous year of study and is unable to move to the next level of their course as a result.
Applicants must live in a low-income household.

Applicants must be ordinarily resident in Scotland at the time of applying and have completed at least two full years of secondary schooling or college education in Scotland, OR be able to demonstrate a substantial and recent connection to Scotland.
Applicants must be entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, have Limited Leave to Remain valid for the entire duration of the course, or be an asylum seeker.
Applicants must not be eligible for public funds (e.g. grants or loans) towards the cost of tuition fees.
Applicants must not have already graduated with a university degree.
Applicants eligible for a SAAS/Student Loans Company maintenance loan are expected to take full advantage of the loans available.

CEF will not consider an application if the student is eligible for support (including loans) from Student Finance England, Wales or Northern Ireland, or any loan or grant from an overseas government or agency.
CEF will generally not fund more than one repeat year for the same course and student.
Applications from students who previously received funding from the Carnegie Education Fund for an undergraduate degree and now wish to start a different course may not be considered.
Part-time students in receipt of tuition fee support from SAAS and not eligible for other grants, bursaries or loans may apply if the SAAS award is less than the total fees payable.
Students who came to Scotland to study at university or college but have no prior education experience in Scotland and no other ties to Scotland will not be considered eligible.
Applications from students who already have a university degree level qualification may be considered exceptionally at the discretion of CEF.

Applicants must have an unconditional offer for, or be a continuing student on, a full-time, part-time or distance learning undergraduate degree course in academic year 2026-27 at a specified Scottish institution or a course validated by a specified university but delivered elsewhere in Scotland.

HNC and HND diploma courses, Access courses, Accelerated degree courses with a graduate entry, courses outside Scotland, courses validated by an overseas university but delivered in Scotland, Open University courses, CPD courses, university courses below degree level, and postgraduate degrees are not eligible for support.

The Carnegie Education Fund has a budget to fund students who completed an undergraduate degree in the past and wish to start a new undergraduate degree in a different field of study in academic year 2026-27.
Students seeking a second undergraduate degree must have completed their first degree at least two years before the start of their new course.
Students seeking a second undergraduate degree must enter the first year of their course in academic year 2026-27.
Students seeking a second undergraduate degree must have been unable to gain employment in their previous degree's subject area, be unemployed, made redundant, or facing redundancy.

Students seeking a second undergraduate degree must wish to reskill in a different field of study, unrelated to previous qualifications, and recognised as being in a skills shortage area for the Scottish economy.

Eligible subject areas for second degrees include Medicine and health, Social work, IT & Computing, Engineering and architecture, Quantitative sciences, Geosciences, Biosciences, and Cultural and creative studies.
Applications are processed on a first come first served basis.
Applicants must take full advantage of SAAS/Student Loans Company loans available to them.
No exceptions or exemptions will be made to any of the eligibility criteria.
Students who have already started a 2nd degree before academic year 2026-27 are not eligible to apply.
The awards cover tuition fees only, up to a maximum of £1,820.
Indicative household income thresholds are provided as guides, with applications reviewed holistically.
The application portal will be open from June 1, 2026, to 5pm on December 1, 2026, for grants covering academic year 2026-27.
An eligibility checker must be completed before applying.
The application form is only accessible during the application window.
Late applications after the closing date will not be accepted, unless the student was first informed that SAAS would not cover their fees after the online portal closed.
Applicants will be notified of the outcome within two to three weeks, provided all requested information and a timely referee response are received.
Supporting documents include evidence of applicant eligibility, a letter of acceptance or enrollment evidence, a SAAS Award Notice letter, and P60 or pay slips/Universal Credit statements.
Students receiving a SAAS bursary must provide a copy of their SAAS award letter.
Supporting evidence can be submitted as scanned copies or mobile images, with a 5MB size limit per file.

claims.text: Funding is available to support postgraduate Master's study.
